steps.title: 2021: grain and steel for the world
text: **Before the full-scale war, [Ukraine](UKR) sold the world mostly food and metals.** It exported $65.8 billion of goods in 2021, and agriculture and food alone made up 40%.
[China](CHN) was its largest customer. The map shows where the exports went.

steps.title: Exports halved within weeks
text: **Two months into the invasion, [Ukraine](UKR)'s exports had halved.** [Russia](RUS) launched its full-scale invasion on 24 February 2022.
Over the whole year exports fell 32%, and the economy shrank by 28.8%.

stat.label: Ukraine's exports in April 2022, compared with April 2021

steps.watch: Watch Ukraine's exports to each partner, month by month, compared with a year earlier.

steps.title: Maize found new buyers
text: **Maize exports held up, but they went to new buyers: [China](CHN)'s share fell from 32% to 17%, and [Romania](ROU) became the largest buyer in the EU.**
From July 2022 to 17 July 2023 the Black Sea Grain Initiative kept three ports near Odesa open for food and fertilizer exports. EU countries are shown separately here.

ask.q: In 2022, which EU country bought the most Ukrainian maize?

steps.watch: Watch the maize arcs swing from China towards the EU.

steps.title: Farm goods became most of what Ukraine sells
text: **Agriculture and food rose from 40% of [Ukraine](UKR)'s exports in 2021 to 59% in 2024**, while base metals shrank to 10% (CEPII BACI).
steps.watch: Watch the product list in the panel re-sort.

steps.title: The EU became the main customer
text: **The [EU](EU)'s share of [Ukraine](UKR)'s exports jumped from 39% in 2021 to 63% in 2022**, after it suspended import duties and quotas on Ukrainian goods from 4 June 2022.

stat.label: The EU's share of Ukraine's exports in 2022

steps.title: Imports came back, exports did not
text: **By 2024 [Ukraine](UKR) imported as much as before the war but exported far less, so its trade deficit grew from $4.1 billion in 2021 to $30.3 billion.**
The highlighted panel section shows the gap opening between exports and imports.
